text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Jordan will not permit any anti-Iraq operations from its territory, King Hussein. The king, in a meeting with General John Shalikashvili, chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff, reiterates support for Iraq's people, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
- Between 30 and 50 face charges in southern riots.
- Jordan expects Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller's visit to boost bilateral ties.
- Ciller, heading a large delegation, to arrive in Amman on Tuesday. Talks will focus on peace, water and bilateral ties.
- Karak deputy Nazih Amareen submits his resignation from parliament but parliamentary sources believe it will not be accepted.
- Information Minister Marwan Muasher says "we will not be a party in any military attack against Iraq".
- Preparations for Arafat-Netanyahu meeting were arranged during telephone call with King Hussein.
- Jordan affirms its support to Iraq's people, territorial integrity.
- Official source says peace process is not on the right track. Jordanian moves aim at telling Israel that it has to execute peace commitments.
- Jordan worried by Iranian involvement in Iraq.
- Opposition launches attack on government. What does the resignation of deputy Amareen mean?.
- Arab Bank posts 65 million dinar profits in first six months of 1996.
